Cockroach Guide

A practical field guide for commercial kitchens, food plants, and facility spaces where warmth, moisture, and harborage create risk.

  1. Home/
  2. Resources/
  3. Cockroach Guide
Facility Guide

What facility teams should watch for

Cockroaches exploit warmth, moisture, and food residue around equipment bases, floor drains, and storage rooms. In commercial settings, early signs usually show up before staff see large numbers of insects.

A strong response combines sanitation corrections, crack-and-crevice treatment, and follow-up monitoring — not one-time spraying alone.

  • Kitchens & food plants
  • Warehouses & break areas
  • Early detection focus
Warning Signs

Common signs of activity

These signals often appear before staff see large numbers of insects — catch them early and pressure is easier to contain.

Droppings

Near appliances, sinks, drains, and baseboards.

Warm motors

Activity around compressors and electrical panels.

Sticky monitors

Live or dead insects in sticky monitors and glue boards.

Egg cases

Oothecae in cracks, hinges, and equipment voids.

Musty odor

In severe or long-running pressure areas.

Night sightings

During night checks or early-morning open.

Where Pressure Builds

Hotspots in commercial facilities

Focus inspections where heat, moisture, and food residue overlap. These areas drive most repeat cockroach pressure.

Kitchens & Prep Areas

Food residue, grease films, and moisture under equipment create reliable harborage.

Floor Drains & Wet Zones

Damp drains, mop sinks, and poorly sealed floor transitions invite overnight travel.

Warm Mechanical Rooms

Motors, panels, and heat sources attract cockroaches seeking shelter during the day.

Storage & Packaging

Cardboard, pallets, and cluttered corners give cover near food and packaging inventory.

Response Steps

Practical next steps for managers

Treat cockroach pressure like a facility process: inspect, correct conditions, then monitor so you know whether activity is falling.

  1. 1
    Step 1

    Inspect Harborage

    Check drains, equipment legs, wall voids, hinges, and warm mechanical areas where cockroaches hide during the day.

  2. 2
    Step 2

    Reduce Attractants

    Improve sanitation around prep areas, trash rooms, and moisture sources so treatments hold longer.

  3. 3
    Step 3

    Treat & Monitor

    Use targeted crack-and-crevice work with follow-up monitoring so activity trends stay visible between visits.
